task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you get your data working again, John. Let me start by pulling up your account.

turns.thought:
I have your account details and updated your line for roaming, but I now need to check some settings directly on your phone.

To begin, please check what's shown at the top of your screen (your status bar) and tell me every icon or symbol you see there. If it's easier, you can describe them in plain words — for example, whether you see little signal bars, "5G" or "4G", a Wi-Fi symbol, an airplane symbol, or anything similar.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at that for you.

turns.thought:
Yes — that "2G" is exactly the problem, and it's great news that we spotted it. 2G is a very old network type that can only handle extremely slow data (and often can't load most apps or web pages at all). Since you're in France, your phone has fallen back to the oldest available network, which explains both the "stopped working" and the "terribly slow" behaviour.

The little **lock symbol (VPN)** is a private network connection — sort of a secure tunnel that all your internet traffic is being routed through. If it's slow or not set up properly, it can slow your data down a lot too, and it isn't needed for your mobile data to work.

Good news on my side already: I've checked your line **555-123-2002**, and I have **turned international roaming on for you** (at no cost). Your line is active, and you've used 8.7 GB out of your 15 GB allowance, so you haven't run out of data.

Now let's fix the phone itself, one small step at a time so it's easy.

**Step 1 — change your phone off that old "2G" network.** Please do this on your phone:
- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Connections** (on some phones it's called **Network & Internet** or just **Mobile Network**)
- Tap **Mobile Networks**, then look for **Network mode** (it may be called "Preferred network mode")
- Choose the option that includes **4G/5G** — for example **"5G/4G/3G auto"** or **"4G/5G preferred"**

Please do that and tell me when it's done (or if you can't find it, just tell me what options you see and I'll guide you). Then we'll deal with the VPN together.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try to find that... I'm poking around in the settings now. I think I found the network mode thing. Let me try changing it to the 4G/5G option.

turns.thought:
Excellent — that's exactly right, well done! Going from "2G / one bar" to "5G / four bars" is the single biggest fix, and you did it yourself. Give yourself a pat on the back.

On the VPN: I understand being nervous, so here's the reassuring part — **you won't be breaking anything**. Turning a VPN off simply means your phone stops routing your internet through that private tunnel and uses your normal mobile connection instead. It can be switched back on just as easily if you ever want it. It doesn't delete anything, and it isn't needed for your mobile data to work here in France.

But let's not change anything until we know it actually needs changing. First, let's measure your data now — this is completely safe and nothing gets changed:

**Please run a speed test on your phone**
- Open your phone's **Settings**
- Go to **Connections** → **Network & Internet** → there should be an option like **Speed test** or **Run speed test** (if you can't find it, just open a browser and try loading any web page instead, and tell me how quickly or slowly it loads)

Once you've done that, tell me:
1. What speed it reports (for example "excellent", "good", "fair", "poor" or "no connection"), and
2. Whether the little lock (VPN) symbol is still showing

With those two answers I'll know for certain whether the VPN is the thing holding you back, and I'll walk you through switching it off step by step if we need to. You're doing great — we're very close.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try that speed test thing.

turns.thought:
You're doing exactly the right thing by telling me — and yes, I understand why that's confusing. Here's what it means in plain terms:

Those four bars and "5G" mean your phone can "see" and talk to the local French network beautifully — that part is now fixed and working. But the speed test saying "no connection" means the actual internet traffic isn't getting through. So the phone-to-network link is good, but something in between is blocking the data. And that little lock (VPN) is now our number one suspect — it's routing all your traffic through a private tunnel that may not be working properly here, which can look exactly like this: great signal, no internet.

There's also a second French-travel possibility I want to check right after this: your phone has a separate "Data Roaming" switch, and when you're abroad it must be ON for data to flow.

Let's deal with the VPN first. It's safe and fully reversible:

**Turn the VPN off**
- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Connections** (or **Network & Internet** on some phones)
- Tap **More connection settings** → **VPN** (on iPhones: **Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → VPN**)
- Next to the VPN that shows "Connected", tap the little **gear/settings ⚙️** icon (on iPhone, tap the **i** or the toggle)
- Choose **Disconnect** (or slide the switch to **Off**)

The lock symbol at the top should disappear once it's off.

**Then please run the speed test again** and tell me the result, and whether the lock symbol is gone.

If it works — wonderful, we're done, and you can switch the VPN back on later if you wish (it just may slow things down here). If it still says no connection, don't worry at all: we'll move straight on to that Data Roaming switch together, and I'll walk you through it step by step just the same. You're nearly there.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll try to turn that VPN thing off. I'm a little nervous but you said it's safe and I can turn it back on. Let me find it...

turns.thought:
I completely understand the frustration — you've done everything right, and it's genuinely puzzling when the fix doesn't work straight away. Please don't lose heart: each thing we've tried has been worth doing, and we've actually ruled out two of the most common causes. That narrows things down nicely, and you were quite right to remember what I said about the Data Roaming switch. That's exactly our next step, and for someone in France it's a very likely culprit.

Here's some good news from my end first: I've already switched international roaming **on for your line** in our system, so our side is ready. Now we just need your phone's own switch to match it — they're two separate things, and both need to be ON.

**Turn on Data Roaming**
- Open **Settings**
- Tap **Connections** (on some phones: **Network & Internet** or **Mobile Network**)
- Tap **Mobile Networks** (or **SIMs** / your phone number)
- Look for **Data roaming** and slide the switch to **ON**
- If your phone asks "Use data while roaming?" or warns about charges, confirm **Allow / Turn On** — your line is roaming-enabled, so this is exactly what we want

**Then run the speed test again** and tell me what it says.

One small tip while you're there: with signal showing "Excellent / 5G", keep your phone near a window if you can — it makes no difference to the settings, but it sometimes helps the phone settle onto the network a touch faster.

If the speed test now shows anything at all — even just "fair" — that's our fix, and you're online. If it still says "No Connection," don't worry for a moment: there are a couple of things I can still check from my side and one more simple setting on your phone, and if we exhaust those, I'll hand you over to our specialist technical team with everything we've tried written up, so you won't have to start over with them. You're very close — let's see what that roaming switch does.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me find that Data Roaming switch. I'm going into the settings... okay, I think I see it. Turning it on now.

turns.thought:
Wonderful — 275 Mbps and "Excellent"! That's a brilliant result, and your patience got you there. Let me answer your questions properly.

**Here's what was actually wrong — it was a combination of three things:**

1. **Your phone was stuck on "2G"**, the oldest (and slowest) network type. You fixed this yourself by choosing "4G/5G preferred" — that's what took you to four bars and 5G.
2. **Data Roaming was switched off on your phone.** Because you're in France, your home network can't carry your data on its own — it has to use a French partner network, and that's exactly what the roaming switch allows. This was the final piece of the puzzle.
3. **The VPN** was also routing all your traffic through a private tunnel, which is a well-known cause of slow or blocked data.

I'd also switched international roaming on for your line on our side earlier on, which your phone needed in order to connect abroad.

**Is it fixed for good?** The settings you changed — the 4G/5G network mode and the Data Roaming switch — stay as they are now. They won't switch themselves back off. So there's nothing more you need to do. Just one small thing worth knowing: the Data Roaming switch needs to stay **ON while you're in France**. When you're back home you can turn it off again if you'd like, though leaving it on causes no harm.

**About the VPN:** leave it off for now — it isn't required for your mobile data to work, and it's one of the things that was interfering. You can switch it back on any time you want, exactly the way you turned it off, and nothing will be lost by it being off.

**About your photos:** turning the VPN off doesn't touch anything stored on your phone — your pictures and videos stay exactly where they are, safe on your device.

**A quick summary of your line, from my side:**
- Line **555-123-2002** is **Active** (nothing suspended)
- International roaming: **ON**
- Data used: **8.7 GB of your 15 GB** allowance, so you have plenty left this cycle
- Your cycle renews on **28 February 2025**

You're all set — enjoy your trip, and those photos of your grandchildren should now send without any trouble at all. If anything changes while you're away, just ask for me again and I'll help you through it step by step.
turns.execution_output:
User: Thank you so much for explaining all of that so clearly. I really appreciate you being patient with me — I know I asked a lot of questions and got a bit flustered there in the middle.

So just to make sure I've got it right: I leave the 4G/5G setting and the roaming switch on while I'm here in France, and I leave the VPN off. And my photos are all safe. That's a relief!

And I've got plenty of data left too, which is good to know. I was a bit worried I'd used it all up with all this testing.

I think we're all done then. Thank you again — you've been ever so kind and I can finally use my phone properly while I'm here. Goodbye now!
